[00:00] Samira Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time, we wanted to run through the joint pipeline and make sure we're aligned on next steps. Uh Diego, you and I will jump in on the technical asks.
[00:18] Karen Liu: Thanks Samira, excited to sync. We have a few deals in flight that the partner team is tracking, and obviously want to understand the deployment story and cost implications.
[00:30] Diego Morales: Hey all. Quick note: I'll be honest, there was a typo in my notes, I wrote "Redwood Deicated" earlier, I meant Dedicated — sorry.
[00:40] Michael Tan: No worries. For timeline context, two of our prospects are targeting pilot starts in August, one in late September. The big asks are latency sub-200ms for chat and strict data residency for one of the regulated accounts.
[01:01] Priya Shah: Right, and on the technical side they asked if we can do VPC peering or fully on-prem installs, and what the roadmap is for KV-cash (sic) sharing between multi-tenant pools.
[01:18] Diego Morales: Yeah, so quick high-level: Redwood supports hosted, dedicated, and private deploy. For the regulated account we'd recommend Private — VPC or on-prem — because of the audit and KMS control needs. For the low-latency chat use-case we can get sub-200ms on Dedicated with proper GPU sizing and batching tweaks, but it depends on concurrency patterns.
[01:45] Ethan Brooks: Can you give a rough cost delta between hosted and dedicated? Exec wants a ballpark to compare unit economics.
[01:54] Samira Patel: Sure. Ballpark, hosted is usually cheaper for low volume but Dedicated gives predictable throughput; think 20-35% premium for Dedicated in our current pricing bands, but I'll have Diego run an estimate on your specific load profiles.
[02:12] Diego Morales: I'll run three scenarios: hosted baseline, dedicated with one reserved pod, and private on a customer-provided cluster. I'll include token cost, infra amortization, and expected latency.
[02:25] Karen Liu: Great. For the pipeline review, let's go line by line. Deal A is with Meridian Health — priority since they want a pilot with PHI. We flagged potential legal hurdles.
[02:40] Ravi Khatri: On legal, we've seen Meridian ask for SOC2 Type II evidence, SAML SSO, audit logs, and KMS integration. We have docs for most of those, I'll link them in the sheet.
[02:53] Michael Tan: Competitor risk here is Anthropic — they have an existing pilot. Meridian is price sensitive and will also ask about model quality/regression protection.
[03:06] Priya Shah: For Meridian's use-case, we recommended Redwood Private with customer-managed KMS, plus RBAC scoped to teams. How long is it to stand up a private deployment?
[03:18] Diego Morales: From kick-off to working pilot usually 4-8 weeks depending on customer's infra readiness. On-prem adds extra time for air-gap validation. We should call out network and storage requirements in the spreadsheet.
[03:32] Karen Liu: Noted. Deal B is with Solaris Financial, less regulated but high QPS, they care more about unit cost and latency. Google Vertex AI is currently in trial there.
[03:43] Samira Patel: For Solaris, Dedicated is often the sweet spot: predictable throughput and better per-token economics at scale, plus we can enable caching to reduce calls. Diego, can you include cache hit-rate assumptions?
[03:56] Diego Morales: Yep — I'll include 0%, 30%, and 60% caching scenarios. Also will add continuous batching effects at 50 RPS vs 200 RPS.
[04:10] Michael Tan: Quick Q — does Redwood support model pinning and automatic fallback to smaller quantized variants? That was a major ask from the ops team.
[04:20] Diego Morales: Yes, model pinning is supported; we also have automated fallback policies for capacity. The runtime can switch to a quantized variant to preserve latency SLOs. Note: I said "quantization-friendly exec paths" in the deck but the transcript might read that strangely.
[04:35] Karen Liu: Good. Deal C is with Nova Retail, they want a POC with embedding-based search and reranking. Not sure which partner motion is best.
[04:46] Samira Patel: For embeddings we have standard pricing and can do a POC on Hosted initially to reduce friction, then shift to Dedicated if they scale. Also we should try to lock down success metrics: increase in NDC (noise down conversion?) sorry, I mean reduction in search latency and improvement in click-through.
[05:03] Karen Liu: (laughs) yes, the auto-transcribe sometimes does wild things.
[05:08] Priya Shah: A note on compliance — Nova wants data retention controls and delete APIs. Do we have that on Hosted?
[05:17] Ravi Khatri: Hosted has configurable retention windows and we provide deletion APIs as part of enterprise plan; for Private the customer controls retention. I'll attach the retention policy page to the sheet.
[05:28] Samira Patel: Alright next, co-sell motions and revenue split — Michael, can you walk through your channel approach?
[05:35] Michael Tan: Sure, typically we prefer a referral + joint-sell where Orion drives the relationship and Redwood provides the tech/ops. For larger deals we discuss referral fees or joint contract models; we prefer to finalize terms once a pilot converts.
[05:50] Samira Patel: Makes sense. We should get legal on a template for a co-sell MOU. Ravi, can your team surface a standard template?
[05:58] Ravi Khatri: I'll share a redline-able MOU template. Note that procurement sometimes wants to see SSO/SAML and SOC2 attachments up front, so let's front-load those.
[06:12] Karen Liu: One more technical ask — Meridian asked about KV-cache sharing across shards; is that supported or will they need custom work?
[06:21] Diego Morales: We support prefix/KV caching per model instance. Cross-shard shared caches are possible but may require additional engineering effort and we should scope that as a small change request. I'll flag it as a potential engineering lift in the notes.
[06:38] Ethan Brooks: On the exec ask, if we run a joint benchmark for Meridian, what do you need from us?
[06:44] Diego Morales: We'll need a representative prompt set, expected concurrency, and sample data shapes. Also access to a staging endpoint and a test account for secure transfer.
[06:55] Samira Patel: Perfect. Wrap up — recap of actions: Samira to update the spreadsheet, Diego to run the latency/cost scenarios, Ravi to share legal template and retention docs, Karen to confirm success criteria and stakeholders.
[07:10] Karen Liu: Yep, and I'll coordinate schedules for the exec briefing.
[07:15] Michael Tan: Let's aim for the exec briefing the week of July 20th, that works for my team.
[07:22] Samira Patel: Works for us — I'll propose time and include a short agenda. Anything else?
[07:28] Priya Shah: Quick note — competitor Anthropic was mentioned by Meridian; we should highlight model quality regressions and our eval hooks in the briefing.
[07:36] Diego Morales: Agreed.
